subject: music
topicDisplay: Area of Study 3: Music for Stage and Screen
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Who composed the music for the musical Wicked, including 'Defying Gravity'?
questions.explain: Stephen Schwartz wrote the music and lyrics for Wicked, the Edexcel set-work source for 'Defying Gravity'.

questions.q: Who composed the music for the film Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope?
questions.explain: John Williams composed the Star Wars score, including the Main Title studied in this Area of Study.

questions.q: In which year did Wicked first open on Broadway?
In which year was Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope released?
questions.explain: Star Wars: A New Hope was released in 1977 with Williams's score.

questions.q: Wicked is based on a novel by which author?
questions.explain: Wicked is based on Gregory Maguire's 1995 novel, a reimagining of the world of The Wizard of Oz.

questions.q: Which composer is most associated with pioneering the use of the leitmotif in opera?
questions.explain: Wagner developed the leitmotif in his operas, an idea later adopted by film composers such as Williams.

questions.q: Which orchestra recorded the original Star Wars soundtrack?
questions.explain: The London Symphony Orchestra recorded Williams's Star Wars score.

questions.q: At which point in Wicked does 'Defying Gravity' appear?
questions.explain: 'Defying Gravity' is the dramatic climax that ends Act 1 of Wicked.

options: A recurring musical theme linked to a character, place or idea
A sudden loud chord used for shock
A section repeated exactly at the end of a piece
A rhythm played only by percussion
questions.explain: A leitmotif is a short recurring theme associated with a specific character, place, emotion or idea.

questions.q: Which character performs 'Defying Gravity' as she resolves to rebel?
questions.explain: Elphaba sings 'Defying Gravity' as she rejects the Wizard and chooses her own path.

questions.q: The Star Wars Main Title theme is most characterised by which feature?
questions.explain: The heroic Main Title opens with a fortissimo brass fanfare over the full orchestra.

questions.q: How does Williams create tension and drama in cues such as the Rebel Blockade Runner music?
options: Simple major triads and a slow waltz
questions.explain: Dissonant harmony, tremolo strings and driving rhythms build suspense and dramatic tension.

questions.q: In which key is the Star Wars Main Title theme?
questions.explain: The heroic Main Title theme is in the bright key of B flat major.

questions.q: Which feature reflects the rock/pop influences in 'Defying Gravity'?
options: A drum kit and electric guitar in the backing band
questions.explain: The pit band includes a rhythm section with drum kit, electric guitar, bass and keyboards, giving a contemporary rock-influenced sound.

questions.q: What is non-diegetic music in a film?
options: Background score that the characters cannot hear
Music a character plays or hears within the scene
Music performed live in the cinema
questions.explain: Non-diegetic music is the underscore heard by the audience but not by the characters on screen.

questions.q: A composer plays the same short brass theme every time a villain appears on screen. This technique is best described as a...
questions.explain: Reusing a recognisable theme to represent a character each time they appear is a leitmotif.

questions.q: To underscore a tense, unresolved chase scene, which device would a film composer most likely use?
options: A quiet perfect cadence held throughout
questions.explain: Dissonance and relentless rhythmic drive create the unsettled, tense mood suited to a chase.

questions.q: A songwriter sets the word 'fly' to a rising melodic line so the music mirrors the meaning. What is this technique called?
questions.explain: Word painting is when the music reflects the meaning of the words, such as a rising line on 'fly'.

questions.q: In a scene, the orchestra plays a quick downward slide exactly as a character trips and falls. This close synchronisation of music to on-screen action is known as...
questions.explain: Mickey-mousing is when the music precisely mirrors and matches the physical action on screen.
